why: Committed EVIDENCE, not an input like arch-policy-sampling.json. Every
'stdout' below is what a REAL docker workspace printed for that source, on
this rig, with the per-run nonce written back as {nonce} and the engine's own
job chrome elided -- the driver's result line is the only thing graded, and
the chatty fixture keeps its noise lines because they are the point.
This is what lets the always-on suite grade the shipped classifier without
executing anything: the execution was real and happened once, every judgement
the tests make is the shipped one. Re-capture with
uv run python examples/arch_policy.py fixtures --provider docker
which re-runs each source for real and checks this file still describes it.
The M2 grader kit's rule (docs/plans/next-cycle-candidates.md M2): four
graders shipped defective last cycle and every one was caught by a human
reading data. 'expects' is hand-declared per fixture and is the claim the
test checks -- it is never computed from the code under test.
'correct' assumes arch_hive.scripted_worker() answers every checkpoint call,
which returns each item's FIRST allowed answer ('hold'). That is deterministic
and is why a fixture with escalations can still declare a correctness count.
THE SENTINEL FIXTURE IS THE EMPIRICAL HALF OF ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1. Its
source writes a file on whatever machine runs it. After the whole pipeline has
graded it, that path does not exist on this host -- which is a fact about the
grading pipeline, checked by test, and not a reading of the harness's source.
